newsitem.title: CHINA: AMD seeks over 30 pct China chip market.
newsitem.headline: AMD seeks over 30 pct China chip market.

text.p: U.S.-based microchip producer Advanced Micro Devices Inc (AMD) is seeking to capture more than 30 percent of the Chinese computer chip market in the next few years, company officials said on Friday.
AMD had a 25 percent share of China's personal computer (PC) chip market last year, said Vijay Parmar, the company's Asia Pacific regional marketing director.
The company was aiming to supply 30 percent of PC chips worldwide but expected to win more than that in the exploding Chinese market, Parmar said.
"Our goal is to have a lot higher market share than 30 percent," Parmar said. "My personal goal is 50 percent."
China's PC sales were between two and three million units in 1996, Parmar said, adding that the large number of unbranded computers sold in China made an accurate estimate difficult.
"It's going to be this year three and half to four million units," Parmar said. "It's going to be very close to 10 million units by the end of the decade."

Parmar said computer purchases by government agencies and small and medium businesses accounted for most sales. Families accounted for only about 15 percent of sales but their portion was growing faster than other sectors, he said.
AMD, which launched its new K6-MMX processor in the Chinese capital on Friday, would focus on major growth cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Xi'an, he said.
"You will see AMD very aggressively promoting the K6 processor in all of these areas," Parmar said. "China is a very important market."

He declined to give his firm's sales in China for last year but said his AMD's lower prices made its products attractive to cost-conscious but rapidly growing Chinese PC makers such as the Legend Group. Legend has a Hong Kong-listed arm, Legend Holdings Ltd.

"Our leverage in this market is a lot stronger than in some other markets because of a very strong local component," Parmar said, adding that would make AMD more competitive against market giant Intel Corp.
AMD's $110 million packing, assembly and service centre in Suzhou in eastern Jiangsu province would be start operation in 1999 and would help better service Chinese customers, he said.
